summary: The comments argue that E-Rate is an ongoing infrastructure requirement for schools, not a one-time project, and that reducing or eliminating E-Rate would shift costs to school districts and compete with other educational priorities. The text argues that E-Rate should not be conditioned on screen-time limits but rather on the actual infrastructure needs of schools. It emphasizes that network requirements are determined by coverage, capacity, and reliability, not by the amount of screen time students spend. The text also highlights the importance of discussing when technology improves learning and when it does not, and how digital assignments affect families.
